title: The Street Where Tourists Risk Their Lives for a Photo
paragraphs: Tourists and influencers like to do risky things to get the perfect photo to share on social media. They might stand on the top of tall buildings or take selfies with wild animals!
In Hanoi, Vietnam, one of the risky places people love to visit is known as Train Street.
You might have seen pictures of it on social media. It's a narrow street in Hanoi's old town with a train track going right through its middle.
Trains pass within touching distance of the homes, cafes and bars that line the street. And tourists flock to the area to experience the thrill of trains passing right in front of their noses.
But as the street has become more popular, it has also become more dangerous.
Since 2017, when its popularity began to grow and locals began making their homes on the street into cafes and bars, the Vietnamese authorities have tried to block off the street to tourists.
That hasn't really worked — large numbers of people still visit to see the trains, which usually pass through twice a day.
Some locals welcome the many visitors, who bring money to the street.
But they also worry that people just come for a photo, and don't learn about the history of the railway and why it's there, and don't learn anything about the culture of the area.
And then of course there is the real danger of the trains. In 2025, a tourist taking a selfie was almost pulled under the wheels of a train.

For now, you'll still see Train Street in social media posts. But this may not last forever: in February 2026, the BBC said the Vietnamese government was thinking about stopping all trains from passing through.
